vector-valued-function.def: A function that gives a vector for each input, such as the position vector $\mathbf{r}(t) = \left\langle x(t), y(t) \right\rangle$ of a moving particle. It describes the same path as the parametric equations $x = x(t)$, $y = y(t)$, and it is differentiated and integrated one component at a time.

velocity-vector.def: The derivative of the position vector, $\mathbf{v}(t) = \mathbf{r}'(t) = \left\langle x'(t), y'(t) \right\rangle$. It is tangent to the path and points in the direction of motion; its magnitude is the speed. The acceleration vector is the next derivative, $\mathbf{a}(t) = \mathbf{v}'(t) = \left\langle x''(t), y''(t) \right\rangle$.
